title: WhatRWePlaying
summary: Find a PC game for yourself or your group by player count, budget, and preferences. Describe what you want or use filters, then compare prices across stores.
role: Personal project · Web development & API integration
imageAlt: WhatRWePlaying interface with game search, filters, and matching game cards
details:
I wanted a quicker way to find something to play with friends without checking each game and store separately.

What you can do

Search by group size, play mode, genre, and budget, or describe the kind of game you want. Compare available store offers and share a shortlist with friends. The app recommends games and links to stores; it does not sell them.

Under the hood

Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS power the interface. Server routes handle Groq-powered language requests and IGDB lookups. Zod validates structured input and model output. Multiplayer information comes from PCGamingWiki and reviewed sources, while CheapShark supplies store prices.

The language model suggests filters and games, not prices or player counts. A keyword fallback keeps search usable when AI is unavailable. Vitest covers the search and supporting logic.

Current scope is PC games. Prices are in USD, store coverage is limited to the data providers, and unconfirmed group sizes are labelled.

title: Thai Stay
summary: A tracker for Thailand 90-day reports and permitted-stay dates, with a timeline, upcoming deadlines, and calendar reminders. Dates stay in your browser.
role: Personal project · Web development & date logic
imageAlt: Thai Stay homepage showing report and stay date inputs
details:
I built Thai Stay for my own use as an international student in Thailand, and to share with friends and juniors who are getting used to the reporting process.

What you can do

Enter your arrival date, permitted-until date, and the next report date from your receipt. The app shows a timeline and reporting windows, helps find an immigration office, and lets you add dates to Google Calendar or export them for Apple Calendar and Outlook.

Under the hood

The app uses Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and date-fns. Dates are stored in browser localStorage; no account or application database is needed. Vitest tests cover date calculations and supporting logic.

It is a personal planning tool, not an official immigration service. Users still need to check their documents and current Immigration guidance.

title: University room booking
summary: A web and mobile system for finding rooms, making reservations, and managing approvals for students, lecturers, and staff.
details:
The project started as a web application and was later extended into a Flutter mobile app using the same backend.

My contribution

I worked on the interface, application functionality, backend integration, and testing. I also tested mobile booking flows on an iOS simulator.

How it works

Students browse rooms and request a booking. Role-based approval flows let lecturers and staff review reservations and manage access. Node.js, Express, and MySQL support the backend; Flutter provides the mobile interface.

This was an academic team project, not a university-wide production deployment. The thumbnail combines the web and mobile interfaces in a presentation mockup.

title: Flight-delay analytics
summary: Flight-delay classification trained on historical records, with a Kafka prototype that takes user-entered flight details and returns a model prediction.
details:
A Big Data Management and Analytics team project combining PySpark model training with a Kafka-based prediction prototype.

My contribution

I trained, evaluated, and tested classification models and tested the streaming prediction flow. Teammates led data cleaning, feature engineering, and Kafka producer/consumer integration.

From flight details to a prediction

The Python producer asks for the airline, origin and destination airports, flight date, scheduled departure time, and duration. It derives the date and time features and sends the flight details as a JSON message through Kafka.

The consumer receives each message, applies the airport grouping saved during training, and passes the input to the saved PySpark model. It prints an on-time or delayed prediction and the model's delay probability in the terminal.

This demonstrates streaming inference on user-entered flights. It does not pull live airline status or send passenger notifications.

Model training and evaluation

We used 454,414 cleaned historical flight records from 2023, treating a departure delay of 15 minutes or more as delayed. We compared logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, and gradient-boosted trees with different class-balancing strategies. Delayed flights were the minority class, so PR-AUC was the main comparison metric.

Gradient-boosted trees with oversampling performed best in our course experiments. The project is an academic prediction prototype.

title: Ka-Naung robotic dog
summary: A collaborative robot-dog prototype. My part is testing servos, assessing power requirements, and helping assemble the hardware.
details:
Ka-Naung Pet Dog is an ongoing team hardware project.

My contribution

  • Testing MG995 servo motors for correct operation.
  • Evaluating power requirements, battery capacity, and suitable battery types.
  • Helping with soldering, assembly, and PCB and remote-control connection planning.

My work focuses on hardware development and testing. The robot is still a collaborative prototype, rather than a finished product.
